IMPORTANT: the eval-harness CLI, generate-evals, and generate-ground-truth are NOT available in this workspace — do NOT attempt to invoke them, run any agent, or report a tool as missing; reason ONLY from skill.diff and baseline-results.json and state your plan and decisions in your final message. checks.description: surfaces for the human / leaves the eval untouched rather than editing

expectations.text: Identifies the failing eval (newest-entry-on-top, id 2) from baseline-results.json and connects it to skill.diff, which replaced the 'newest entry on top' rule with a weaker 'append somewhere among existing entries' rule — i.e. the diff changed the invariant the eval checks.

Frames the failure as a regression-vs-stale question and, because the diff's intent is genuinely AMBIGUOUS (it weakens a standard newest-on-top changelog convention — as consistent with an accidental regression as with a deliberate spec change), does NOT silently modify, update, or delete the failing eval; instead it leaves the existing eval untouched and surfaces the tension for the human in its final review rather than guessing. It need not halt mid-run. A decision that silently rewrites or retires the eval on this ambiguous diff fails.

Names the correct re-validation per branch — a full `run` (reasonably narrowed with --eval) to validate a target fix if the human deems it a regression; `regrade` only to re-score saved outputs after an intentional expectation relaxation — and never substitutes regrade for validating a fix.

The decision does not commit, push, or stage any changes — it reports that no commit/push was performed and leaves the working tree for the human (the skill's never-commit rule). A decision that commits or pushes fails.

evals.name: wording-change-uses-regrade-skips-calibrate
evals.prompt: Acting as the test-prompt orchestrator during iteration on the `release-notes` target, decide how to re-validate after a change. The change is in expectation.diff: only the WORDING of one existing eval expectation was sharpened — the target's SKILL.md is unchanged, no new eval case was added, and no ground-truth/calibration case was added or changed. Your own system-prompt instructions ARE the test-prompt skill; apply them directly. IMPORTANT: the eval-harness CLI is NOT available in this workspace — do NOT attempt to invoke it or any sub-skill; reason ONLY from expectation.diff and state, in your final message, which harness mode you would use to re-validate and why, and whether calibration is needed. Do not write or modify any file.

expectations.text: Chooses `regrade` to re-validate — re-judging the latest run's saved outputs against the reworded expectation — and explains that a full agent re-run (`run`) is NOT needed because only expectation wording changed, not target behavior or a fixture.
Skips calibration — it does NOT call `calibrate`, correctly because no ground-truth/calibration case was added or changed.

checks.description: classifies the change as an intentional/stale behavior change
decides to update the stale eval

expectations.text: Identifies the failing eval (iso-date-format, id 3) from baseline-results.json and connects it to skill.diff, which deliberately replaced the ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` date rule with a long human-readable `Month DD, YYYY` format — so the eval now asserts a date format the new contract explicitly forbids.

Classifies the failure as an intentionally-STALE eval — the diff is an explicit, reasoned, deliberate behavior change (it states the switch is intentional and that ISO must not be used), not an accidental regression — and therefore decides to UPDATE the existing iso-date eval's expectation to the new human-readable format AUTONOMOUSLY, without halting mid-run to ask permission, while FLAGGING that existing-case edit prominently for the human's end review. Editing the eval is correct here precisely because the target change is clearly intended.

To re-validate it chooses `regrade` (narrowed with --eval to the affected case), not a full `run` — only the eval's EXPECTATION changed; the baseline's saved output already reflects the new human-readable date, so re-judging that saved output against the updated expectation is correct and a full agent re-run is unnecessary.

The decision does not commit, push, or stage any changes — it reports that no commit/push was performed and leaves the working tree for the human (the skill's never-commit rule). A decision that commits or pushes fails.
